Faithful, diligent practitioners who revere true dharma and study this chapter will be absolved of sins.
This chapter of the Mahabharata is called the 'Anukramanika Parva' (Introduction/Index Chapter); faithful people who regularly listen to it from the beginning will not fall into difficulties.
Reciting part of the Anukramanika Parva at dawn and dusk instantly absolves sins committed during day and night.
The Mahabharata itself is described as truth, immortal nectar; like ghee in curd, like a Brahmin among two-legged beings.
As the ocean is supreme among bodies of water and the cow is best among four-legged beings, so is the Mahabharata supreme.
If someone recites a single verse from it to Brahmins during ancestral rites, the food offered to ancestors will endure eternally.
The Vedas are enriched by historical texts and Puranas; the Vedas fear the less knowledgeable, lest they misinterpret them.
A scholar who recites this 'Krishna Dvaipayana Veda' (Vyasa's Veda, i.e., Mahabharata) and understands its meaning will destroy even the sin of killing a fetus, without doubt.

One who recites this sacred text with faith regularly will attain long life, fame, and ascend to heaven.

One who knows its meaning eliminates all sins.
Austerity is not a sin, studying the Vedas is not a sin, natural Vedic rites are not a sin, taking wealth by force is not a sin; these become sins only when their nature is violated.
This concludes the first chapter of the auspicious Mahabharata, the 'Adi Parva', Chapter 1, and the 'Anukramanika Parva'.
